stage_description: The mature adult is 7 to 10 years old (AAHA/AAFP 2021), the feline equivalent of middle age. The cat may still look active, but this is when hidden chronic conditions begin — obesity, diabetes, early kidney disease, and arthritis. Regular weight monitoring and screening tests at this stage catch problems before obvious symptoms appear.
nutrition: An adult or purpose-formulated diet with calorie control; maintaining an ideal body condition matters most here. Where problems are found (joints, kidneys, weight), use therapeutic diets on veterinary advice, and ensure adequate water intake.
activity: Regular moderate activity and mental stimulation — new toys, food puzzles, and safe vantage points. Keeping the cat active helps control weight and preserve joint mobility.
veterinary_check_frequency: An exam once a year, ideally transitioning to visits every 6 months with baseline blood chemistry, urinalysis, blood-pressure checks, and thyroid assessment to catch age-related disease early.
dental_care: Regular home brushing and a professional oral assessment; periodontal disease and tooth resorption are common and painful in cats, so cleaning is done as indicated.
warning_signs: Increased thirst and urination (diabetes, kidney disease), weight loss with a preserved appetite, litter-box changes, or reduced activity or mobility. These signs warrant a veterinary evaluation.
disclaimer: This information is for educational purposes only and does not replace consultation with a veterinarian.
